recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Migration: add reverses_request_id to leave_requests
recommended_phases.rationale: New knex migration `migrations/<ts>_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js`: `alterTable('leave_requests', t => { t.text('reverses_request_id'); t.index(['reverses_request_id']); })`, `down()` drops the index then the column. Nullable text (matches the initial-schema text style and the password_hash precedent), no FK to keep the migration portable across pg/sqlite3. Must land first: every later phase reads/writes the column. No source files touched.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — leave model + repository: reversesRequestId end-to-end
recommended_phases.rationale: `leave.model.ts`: add `reversesRequestId: string | null` to `LeaveRequest` (CreateLeaveRequestInput follows via Omit). `leave.repository.ts`: add `reverses_request_id` to `LeaveRequestRow`, `COLUMNS`, `mapRow`, the INSERT column/value list (15 values), and `FIELD_COLUMNS` (`reversesRequestId: 'reverses_request_id'`); add `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId, client?)` to `ILeaveRepository` + `PgLeaveRequestRepository` (`WHERE reverses_request_id = $1`) so the service can detect an existing reversal. `leave.service.ts` `create` supplies `reversesRequestId: null`. Depends only on Phase 1.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — LeaveService.cancel: reversal branch for APPROVED
recommended_phases.rationale: In `cancel`, split the terminal write by status inside the existing single `uow.withTransaction`: DRAFT/SUBMITTED keep the in-place `repository.update(... status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt ...)` exactly as today; APPROVED instead (a) checks `findByReversesRequestId(requestId, client)` and throws ConflictError if a reversal already exists (release-exactly-once guard), (b) releases `usedDays -= requestedDays` on the locked balance row, (c) `repository.create({ ...original fields copied ..., status: CANCELLED, reversesRequestId: requestId, cancelledBy: actor.id, cancelledAt: now })` leaving the original row untouched, (d) writes the CANCEL audit entry with `entityId` = the NEW row id and `beforeState` = the original APPROVED row, (e) notifies the requester. The returned value is the new CANCELLED row. No route change needed — `reversesRequestId` serializes with the model on GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Unit tests: reversal immutability + single release
recommended_phases.rationale: Extend `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts` (existing eight fakes; `FakeLeaveRepository` gains `findByReversesRequestId` and records `create` calls). Assert: after cancelling an APPROVED request the original row is never passed to `update` and still reads APPROVED with its approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt unchanged; a new row is created with `status CANCELLED` and `reversesRequestId === original.id`; `usedDays` is decremented exactly once by `requestedDays`; exactly one CANCEL audit entry; one notification; all inside one `withTransaction` callback with the stub client forwarded. Plus the DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place paths unchanged and the duplicate-reversal ConflictError. Depends on Phase 3.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Smoke: real-Postgres reversal proof
recommended_phases.rationale: Extend `scripts/smoke.js` (Postgres mode): seed an APPROVED request with a balance row, `POST /leaves/:id/cancel`, then assert `GET /leaves/:id` on the original still returns `status APPROVED` with its approverId/decidedAt intact, that `GET /leaves` contains a second row with `status CANCELLED` and `reversesRequestId === original.id`, and that `GET /balances/me` shows `usedDays` released exactly once. This is the acceptance test the feature names. Depends on Phases 1–3.

app_notes:
## Scope

GP-008 reversal. One module changes (`leave`), plus one migration. No new module, no new endpoint, no new cross-module edge — the dependency map is unchanged from the reconciled architecture and is acyclic (leave -> {balance, audit, notification, employee, validation, policy, shared-*}; balance -> {policy, employee, shared-*}; policy/employee/audit/notification/validation -> shared-* only; nothing depends back on leave).

## Layer boundaries

- **presentation** — `src/modules/*/*.routes.ts` (Fastify handlers, `resolveActor`, `sendError`). No controller layer (open question Q1, resolved: routes call services directly).
- **application** — `ILeaveService`/`LeaveService` (orchestration, transaction boundary, authorization, audit/notification side effects). This is the only layer this feature touches.
- **domain** — `LeaveRequest` model + `LeaveStatus` lifecycle; `requestedDays` in `src/shared/types`.
- **infrastructure** — `ILeaveRepository`/`PgLeaveRequestRepository`, `IBalanceRepository`, `IUnitOfWork`/`PgUnitOfWork`, `migrations/`.

Dependencies flow inward only. `LeaveService` depends on repository *interfaces* and `IUnitOfWork`, never on `pg` or SQL (GP-001).

## Binding semantics for this feature

1. **Immutability (GP-008).** For an APPROVED request, `cancel` MUST NOT call `repository.update` on the original row. The original's `status`, `approverId`, `approvalComment`, `decidedAt` are frozen. The reversal is a NEW `leave_requests` row with `status = CANCELLED` and `reversesRequestId = <original id>`.
2. **DRAFT/SUBMITTED unchanged.** Those two states keep the existing in-place `update` to CANCELLED. No completed approval exists, so GP-008 does not apply.
3. **Release exactly once.** The `usedDays -= requestedDays` release happens in the SAME `uow.withTransaction` as the reversal insert, computed from the ORIGINAL row's `requestedDays` (never the reversal row's). The balance row is read with `forUpdate = true` before the write. A second cancel of the same APPROVED request must not release again — guarded by `findByReversesRequestId(requestId, client)` inside the transaction, throwing `ConflictError` when a reversal already exists. This is the BR-001 anti-pattern guard: the release rule lives in one place and every path that could reach it is specified.
4. **Audit (GP-002).** The CANCEL audit entry is still written, inside the same transaction, with `entityId` = the NEW reversal row's id and `beforeState` = the original APPROVED row (so the audit trail shows the frozen state that was reversed).
5. **Wire honesty.** `reversesRequestId` is a field on the leave-owned `LeaveRequest` model, so it serializes automatically on `GET /leaves` and `GET /leaves/:id`. No route change is required. A cancelled-after-approval leave is now two rows and the client can tell which is which.

## Shared-type placement (applied mechanically)

`reversesRequestId` is a field on `LeaveRequest`, which is owned by the `leave` module and used by exactly one module — so it stays in `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts`. It is NOT a cross-module value type and must NOT be moved to `src/shared/types/`. `LeaveStatus` (already in `src/shared/types/`) is unchanged — no new enum member is needed, since the reversal reuses `CANCELLED`. `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` gains `reversesRequestId?: string` only if the repository's `FIELD_COLUMNS` map is extended to allow updating it; the recommended design does not update it (it is set once at insert), so `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` is left alone.

## Transaction contract

`LeaveService.cancel` owns the boundary via `IUnitOfWork.withTransaction`. `PgUnitOfWork` is the only place BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK appear. Every participating call takes an optional trailing `PoolClient` and joins the caller's transaction: `ILeaveRepository.findByReversesRequestId`, `ILeaveRepository.create`, `IBalanceRepository.findByKey` (with `forUpdate`), `IBalanceRepository.update`, `IAuditService.record`, `INotificationService.create`. Repositories never open a transaction.

## Phase ordering rationale

Migration first (the column must exist before any code reads it), then model+repository (the persistence contract), then the service branch (the only behavior change), then unit tests, then the real-Postgres smoke proof. Each phase is a small, self-contained diff well inside Aider's effective context window; no phase requires reading more than three source files plus one test file.

open_questions.question: What should the reversal row's `requestedDays` be — a copy of the original's day count, or 0?
open_questions.impact: Any future aggregate over `leave_requests` (a per-employee total, a report, a dashboard sum) double-counts the leave if the reversal row copies `requestedDays`. The balance release itself is unaffected (it uses the ORIGINAL row's `requestedDays`), so the choice is invisible to this feature's acceptance test but silently wrong for every later consumer.
candidate_options: Copy the original's requestedDays onto the reversal row (the row is a faithful snapshot of what was reversed; aggregates must filter by status/reversesRequestId)
Set the reversal row's requestedDays to 0 (the reversal consumed no leave; aggregates stay naive-correct)
Copy requestedDays but add a binding rule that every aggregate must exclude rows where reversesRequestId IS NOT NULL

open_questions.question: Should GET /leaves return reversal rows by default, or only when explicitly requested?
open_questions.impact: The feature requires the read model to expose `reversesRequestId` so a client can tell the two rows apart, which implies both rows are returned. But a client that lists "my leave requests" now sees two entries for one cancelled-after-approval leave, and any client-side count or total is wrong unless it filters. The wire contract is honest either way; the default is what decides whether existing clients silently double-count.
candidate_options: Return both rows always (reversesRequestId is the discriminator; clients filter) — matches the stated requirement literally
Return both rows but add a `reversesRequestId` query filter so a client can request only originals
Exclude reversal rows from GET /leaves by default and expose them only via GET /leaves/:id

open_questions.question: Which fields does the reversal row copy from the original — and does it carry its own approverId/decidedAt?
open_questions.impact: The original's approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt are immutable and must not be touched, but the NEW row's own values are unspecified. If the reversal row copies approverId/decidedAt it looks like a second approval decision in any audit or reporting query; if it leaves them null it loses the link to who decided the leave it reverses (recoverable only by joining through reversesRequestId).
candidate_options: Copy employeeId/leaveTypeCode/startDate/endDate/requestedDays/reason; leave approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt null on the reversal row (the reversal is a cancellation, not a decision)
Copy every field including approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt so the reversal row is a full snapshot
Copy the leave fields and set approverId = actor.id with decidedAt = now (the canceller is recorded as the decider of the reversal)

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role are obtained from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing registerAuth preHandler (src/shared/auth/index.ts), which populates request.user from payload.sub (id) and payload.role. RBAC is enforced at the API boundary by resolveActor (presence + EmployeeRole membership, UnauthorizedError otherwise) and in the service by assertCanCancel — never inline in the route handler (GP-005). Cancellation authority is unchanged by this feature: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; an APPROVED request may be cancelled only by the requester's direct manager (employee.managerId === actor.id) or an ADMIN (exempt from the direct-manager check). No new endpoint and no new role is introduced; POST /leaves/:id/cancel already exists and keeps its guard.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string } via the existing sendError helper in leave.routes.ts. Validation failure -> HTTP 400 (ValidationError, code VALIDATION); authentication failure -> 401 (UnauthorizedError, code UNAUTHORIZED); authorization failure -> 403 (ForbiddenError, code FORBIDDEN); not found -> 404 (NotFoundError, code NOT_FOUND); invalid state transition -> 409 (ConflictError, code CONFLICT); any other throw -> 500. This feature adds one 409 case: cancelling an APPROVED request that already has a reversal row throws ConflictError (the release-exactly-once guard). GET /leaves/:id keeps its information-hiding contract — a request the caller may not see returns the byte-identical 404 as a nonexistent id. No new endpoint is added, so no new status code is introduced.
